prompt: Lay out a debugger watch panel as aligned text, truncating values that are too long. Complete WatchTableFormatter, then run the tests.
explanation: Aligning a column needs two passes: the first finds the widest expression, and only then can the second pass know how much padding each row needs. " ".repeat(width - length) supplies exactly that padding, so every "=" lands in the same column. truncate keeps the 17 + "..." split so a cut value is still exactly 20 characters wide and the table never ragged, and handling null there rather than in format keeps the null check in one place. Throwing IllegalArgumentException on mismatched sizes fails loudly instead of silently formatting half a table.
hints: You cannot format the first row until you know the longest expression -- loop over the expressions once to find the width before building any rows.
" ".repeat(n) builds the padding; the row is expression + padding + " = " + truncate(value).
Check the two sizes and throw IllegalArgumentException before doing any work at all.
